at: Yushin does not answer the count.
alt: Rodin’s Thinker, painted: Yushin as a green-patinated bronze on a granite block before the council hall steps
scene: A painted parody of Auguste Rodin’s THE THINKER: an oil painting of the bronze statue, thick visible brushstrokes, dark bronze body with green-and-gold patina painted in broad strokes, simplified heroic forms, on a rough granite block. Exact Thinker pose: seated, hunched forward, RIGHT elbow on the LEFT thigh, chin propped on the back of the right hand, left forearm across the left knee, feet planted, brow furrowed. The statue is KIM YUSHIN, face from the attached portrait, cast as bronze, wearing his marshal’s robe and topknot as bronze folds (clothed, not nude), no sword. The block stands at the foot of the stone steps of a Silla council hall, timber pillars and grey giwa roof dissolving into brushwork, deep blue #2A5FB8 dusk sky.

alt: The keynote, painted: Chunchu alone on a black stage in one hard spotlight, holding up a small bronze seal, a giant ink circle on the screen behind
scene: A painted parody of the famous STEVE JOBS keynote photograph, as a painterly anime-adjacent illustration with visible brushwork: pitch-black stage, one hard white spotlight, a huge glowing projection screen behind. Same staging: the presenter alone near the stage edge, relaxed, holding one small object up between thumb and fingers at shoulder height, other hand open, easy half-smile. The presenter is KIM CHUNCHU (attached portrait: face, magenta #D8258C Silla court silk, topknot), holding up a small square bronze seal as if it were the new product. The screen shows only one black ink-brush circle on white. Silhouetted heads of officials in black gat hats in the foreground.

alt: The green-jacket ceremony, painted: Alchun holding open a green silk coat while Pumsuk shrugs into it, polo stick in hand
scene: A painted parody of the MASTERS GREEN-JACKET CEREMONY photo, as a painterly anime-adjacent illustration with loose brushwork: bright afternoon, blurred painted crowd and pines behind. Same staging: last year’s champion stands behind the winner holding open a green jacket while the winner slips one arm into the sleeve, both grinning stiffly at unseen cameras. At the edge of a Silla gyuku (polo) field: ALCHUN (attached portrait: face and garments) holds open a bright GREEN silk Silla coat; PUMSUK (attached portrait: face, sky-blue #7EB8F0 silk) shrugs into it, flushed and cocky, a polo stick in his other hand with presentation silk still wrapped on its head. Painted horses and nobles in hanbok behind.

alt: The unit class photo, painted: the new Hwarang intake in stiff rows on the hall steps, Bupmin front and centre, Yushin at the end with his arms folded
scene: A painted parody of a Korean MILITARY UNIT CLASS PHOTO (기수 사진), as a painterly anime-adjacent illustration with a warm faded palette, visible brushwork, a painted white print border. Same staging: dead-frontal symmetrical group on stepped risers, three rows, front row seated with fists on knees, back rows at attention, everyone staring stiffly out, one instructor rigid at the end. Teenage Hwarang cadets in matching headbands and practice silk on the stone steps of a Silla training hall with timber pillars and a grey giwa roof: one blinking, one grinning, one with a black eye. BUPMIN (attached portrait: face and garments) dead centre in the front row. YUSHIN (attached portrait: face, marshal blue #2A5FB8) stands at the right end, arms folded, no sword.

alt: Abbey Road, painted: young Bidam, Alchun and Yushin crossing a stream on stepping stones in single file, mid-stride
scene: A painted parody of THE BEATLES’ ABBEY ROAD album cover, as a square painterly anime-adjacent illustration with soft summer light and visible brushwork. Same staging: exactly three young men walking in single file left to right in strict side profile, evenly spaced, all mid-stride with the same leg forward, a leafy street receding behind. The zebra crossing is a straight row of flat pale granite stepping stones (징검다리) across a shallow stream beside a Silla yard wall with grey giwa, willows behind. BIDAM leads (attached Hwarang portrait, black headband), ALCHUN in the middle (attached portrait, drawn younger), YUSHIN last (attached Hwarang portrait, blue headband), wide silk sleeves swinging, no swords. Navy #141C2E in the willow shade.

at: of his own sons to the Assembly
alt: 12.12: The Day, painted: Euija grinning at the centre of his victory portrait, the forty-one sons he just seated packed in rows around him on the palace steps
scene: A painted parody of the victory group photo that ends the Korean coup film 12.12: THE DAY (the conspirators’ commemorative portrait the night the coup succeeds), as a painterly anime-adjacent illustration with the film’s teal-and-amber grade and visible brushwork. Same staging: a dense, stiff, frontal group portrait on the steps of a government building at night, the ringleader dead centre in the front row grinning wide, the co-conspirators packed shoulder to shoulder in rising rows, smug, some clapping, one flash-lit. Here: KING EUIJA (attached portrait: face and garments) sits front and centre, laughing, amber #e08a2e lamplight on his face; around and behind him FORTY-ONE of his sons, young men and boys in new Baekje court robes and black hats, in five packed rows on the stone steps of the attached Sabi palace hall (red pillars, giwa eaves). At the edge, a row of empty lacquered Assembly chairs pushed aside.

alt: Team 7’s photo as the Three Eternal Hwarang: Yushin and Bidam glaring at each other, Alchun grinning in the middle, Princess Dukman behind with a hand on each rival’s head
scene: A parody of the NARUTO TEAM 7 PHOTO (the framed picture on the bedside table), painted as bright anime key art with clean cel shading and a slightly faded framed-photo feel. Same staging: three young teammates in front, the teacher standing behind them. On the left the loud one glares sideways at the rival with fists clenched; on the right the cool prodigy looks away with arms crossed, glaring back; the one in the middle beams at the camera with hands clasped; the teacher behind rests a hand on top of each rival’s head, eyes creased in a smile. Here, as teenage Hwarang of Class 51 in a Silla training yard with a grey giwa wall and a gyuku stick on the ground: YUSHIN on the left (attached Hwarang portrait, blue #2A5FB8 headband), BIDAM on the right (attached Hwarang portrait, black headband, navy #141C2E robe), ALCHUN in the middle (attached portrait, drawn as a teenager, grinning). Behind them young PRINCESS DUKMAN (attached portrait: face and silk) with a hand on each boy’s head, amused. Tied cloth headbands, no metal plates, no ninja symbols.

at: shatters the Wa army besieging Silla
alt: The Alexander Mosaic in tesserae: Gwanggaeto bareheaded on horseback charging through a forest of spears, the Wa commander twisting in flight
scene: A parody of the ALEXANDER MOSAIC from Pompeii (the Battle of Issus), made exactly like the real Roman floor mosaic: thousands of small stone tesserae, limited palette of ochre, brick red, black, white and grey, patches of missing tiles, a dark broken border. Same composition: on the left the young conqueror charges on horseback, bareheaded, eyes wide, spearing an enemy; on the right the enemy leader, in a chariot, twists back in horror and flings out an arm as his army turns to flee; a forest of long spears slanting across the sky; a bare dead tree. The conqueror is GWANGGAETO (attached portrait: face) in gray steel lamellar (attached ref) with a red #e0442e cloak; the fleeing leader is a Wa commander in lacquered plate on a boat-shaped chariot, Wa foot soldiers scattering.

alt: Ingres’ Napoleon on His Imperial Throne: Gwanggaeto frozen frontal on a round-backed throne, red and gold, sceptre and bow in hand
scene: A parody of Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres’ NAPOLEON I ON HIS IMPERIAL THRONE, painted exactly like the real canvas: enamel-smooth Neoclassical oil, icy precision, stiff hieratic frontality like a Byzantine icon, a huge round gilded throne back framing the head like a disc, heavy fabrics, patterned carpet at the feet. Same pose: seated dead-frontal, expressionless, a long sceptre upright in the right hand, a rod in the left, heavy robes spilling over the knees. The emperor is GWANGGAETO (attached portrait: face) in Goguryeo red #e0442e and gold court robes with a gold crown of flame-shaped uprights; the round throne back carries a painted three-legged crow in a sun disc; a strung horn bow leans on the throne; the carpet shows a pattern of tiny fortress walls.

at: crown princes go north as hostages
alt: Vercingetorix Throws Down His Arms at the Feet of Caesar: a Silla crown prince rides in and drops his sword before Gwanggaeto’s dais
scene: A parody of Lionel Royer’s VERCINGETORIX THROWS DOWN HIS ARMS AT THE FEET OF JULIUS CAESAR, painted exactly like the real 1899 academic oil canvas: polished Salon realism, warm grey sky, crisp drawing, rows of armored soldiers with standards. Same composition: the conqueror sits on a raised dais at the right, stern, surrounded by his officers and standards; from the left a young defeated leader on a white horse rides up and throws his weapons down on the ground at the foot of the dais, head high. The conqueror is GWANGGAETO (attached portrait: face) in gray steel lamellar (attached ref) and a Goguryeo helm (attached kingdom ref, ignore labels) with red #e0442e cloak and red wing shoulder-flaps; the rider is a young SILLA CROWN PRINCE in white silk and a small gold crown, dropping a ring-pommel sword and a bow. Goguryeo spearmen, banners with a three-legged crow.

at: does not do him the courtesy of bending
alt: Odysseus’ bow on a red-figure cup: Tabal straining at Jumong’s bow while Jumong lounges and grins
scene: A parody of the ODYSSEY bow contest (the suitors failing to string Odysseus’ bow), painted exactly like a real Attic RED-FIGURE kylix tondo: a circular cup interior, figures reserved in orange terracotta against glossy black slip, fine black relief lines for folds and muscles, a meander key border around the circle, small chips and a museum-lit sheen. In the circle: a heavy older chieftain braced with one foot on the bow, veins bulging, straining to bend it, the string slack; beside him a young man lounges on a stool, clean-shaven, grinning, chin on his hand. The chieftain is YEON TABAL (attached portrait 1, face); the young man is JUMONG (attached portrait 2, face; clean-shaven, no mustache). A torch and a pine-branch in the field. Jumong’s cloak picked out in added red #e8563f.

at: He splits Tabal’s arrow down the shaft.
alt: Odysseus’ arrow on a black-figure amphora: Jumong at full draw, his arrow threading a row of iron rings to split Tabal’s arrow in the pine knot
scene: A parody of Odysseus shooting through the twelve axe-heads, painted exactly like a real archaic Greek BLACK-FIGURE AMPHORA (Exekias style): a photographed pot shape, glossy black silhouette figures on orange clay, incised details scratched through the black, added red and white touches, tongue-pattern bands above and below the picture panel. In the panel: a young archer in profile at full draw, clean-shaven, knee bent; his arrow flies through a straight row of twelve small iron rings on posts and strikes a pine tree, splitting another arrow already lodged in the knot. The archer is JUMONG (attached portrait: face in profile, clean-shaven, no mustache), with added red #e8563f on his tunic.

alt: Laocoön, painted: Bidam as a marble figure writhing in the coils of Hyullé’s water-serpent, beads flying
scene: A painted parody of the LAOCOÖN GROUP marble sculpture: an oil painting of the white marble statue, broad creamy brushstrokes, cool grey shadows, dramatic raking light on a dark ground. Same pose: a muscular man twisting in agony on an altar block, one arm flung up and back, torso straining, head thrown back, a huge serpent coiling around his legs and arm and biting at his hip. The man is BIDAM (attached portrait: face with thin mustache and swept grey hair, carved in marble), nude but for a marble cloth at the hips, a string of prayer beads snapping in his raised hand. The serpent is the water goddess Hyullé’s serpent form: its scales painted wet teal #2eb8c4 over the marble, water spilling off the coils.

at: raised a tower to read the stars
alt: The Gwanghwamun King Sejong statue, painted: Queen Sunduk as the gilded seated monument, book open, Cheomseongdae rising behind her
scene: A painted parody of the KING SEJONG STATUE at Gwanghwamun: an oil painting of the huge gilded bronze monument seen from a low angle on its broad stone plinth, thick brushwork, gold catching late sun. Same pose: a monarch seated on a throne, calm and benevolent, an open book resting in the left hand, the right hand extended palm-down in a gesture of blessing, heavy royal robes cascading. The monarch is QUEEN SUNDUK (attached portrait: face; hair ornament matching the attached binyeo ref) as gilded bronze, her robes tinted vermilion #E8552B under the gold. Behind the plinth rises the bottle-shaped stone observatory tower Cheomseongdae from the attached place ref, under a deepening blue evening sky with first stars.

at: cuts a rank the grades did not have
alt: The Gwanghwamun Admiral Yi statue, painted: old Yushin as the towering bronze general, ring-pommel sword planted, Pyongyang’s walls behind
scene: A painted parody of the ADMIRAL YI SUN-SIN STATUE at Gwanghwamun: an oil painting of the towering dark bronze monument seen from a steep worm’s-eye angle on its tall stone pedestal, thick brushwork, bronze glinting. Same pose: a standing general in armor, feet apart, looking far ahead, a long sword held upright in front of him in its scabbard, both hands resting on it. The general is the old KIM YUSHIN (attached old portrait: face, white beard) in bronze steel lamellar (attached ref), marshal-blue #2A5FB8 cloth peeking at the collar as patina; the sword is the attached ring-pommel 환두대도, small ring pommel up. Behind the pedestal, the red two-tier gate pavilion and stone walls of the attached Pyongyang fortress under a wide autumn sky.

at: Like the three hundred at Thermopylae
alt: The 300 poster, painted: Gyebek mid-roar behind a round shield, spear up, red cloak whipping, the five thousand behind him in a sepia storm
scene: A parody of the film poster for 300 (Frank Miller’s graphic-novel look), painted as a gritty high-contrast illustration: sepia-bronze storm sky, crushed blacks, desaturated skin, only the cloak saturated, dust and grain, no lettering. Same layout: the king in the foreground roaring, mouth wide open, round shield braced on one arm and spear raised, blood-red cloak whipping behind him, a packed line of warriors behind with shields locked. The king is GYEBEK (attached portrait: face), in gray steel lamellar (attached ref) with yellow #d9b13a cloth at collar and sleeves and a red cloak, his round shield painted with a phoenix; behind him the five thousand Baekje spearmen, yellow dust rising off the Yellow Mountain.

alt: The Godfather poster, painted: Chunchu’s hand in a magenta sleeve holding the marionette bar, the Harmony Council dangling in their polished chairs
scene: A parody of THE GODFATHER film poster, painted: a pure black field, and from the top edge a single hand holding a wooden marionette control bar, white strings falling straight down; no lettering at all. Same layout and stark minimalism. The hand comes out of a magenta #D8258C Silla silk sleeve (KIM CHUNCHU, attached portrait: garments; his face half-visible in shadow at the very top, amused). On the strings hang tiny wooden puppets of grey-bearded True Bone councillors, each sitting in a little polished lacquered chair, arms lifted as if voting. Painterly, graphic, high contrast.
